checks: On the admitted interval J and R are positive increasing; y increases, and z,w increase because G−K,D−K are strictly below one. Only at actual sum-one roots does this force x to decrease. Thus all three positive raw ratios strictly decrease between the roots.

The signs A>0≥B in the actual centroid identities imply Kx>N≥Ky and hence q>1. Relabeling is valid for any other strict split with the same one noncentral coordinate, since both opposite coordinates are automatically strictly below 1/3.

Signs are unchanged on the segment and on the ray beyond the smaller root away from the larger. On the other ray, requiring vertex 2 negative, vertex 3 margin greater than one and vertex 4 negative gives the exact open interval. Strict signs exclude equality endpoints.

The larger-K chart point is strictly between the two other points on the line. Since every chart first coordinate is one, its coefficient has the unique opposite sign in every nonzero dependence. A positive dependence of raw oriented margins transfers this sign distinction to their orientations.

dependencies.hypotheses: Uses its exact positive interval, monotonicity of J and R, recovery equations, and the two actual sum-one roots. The proof does not assume that raw ratios are monotone away from the roots. The frozen predecessor needs independent approval before this result can be admitted.

overlap.comparison: Controls dependence of three planes sharing the same split, with a two-root count in the equal-opposite-coordinate case. It gives neither the actual-root ordering nor the necessary condition for a third plane of a different split.

readability: The final interval is necessary for the indicated different split; it does not establish existence of the third section.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: The ordering holds on the two actual normalized roots and yields the claimed necessary ray, interval and orientation condition for a third actual cross-split section.
